Date: 2028-05-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sentinel stability: tokens -> SLO breakdown and GPU allocation

Hi Lina —

Per our call this morning, attached is a pragmatic breakdown that ties the committed token run-rate to p95 latency and the resulting GPU slab recommendation. High-level summary up front:

- Target p95 latency: 250ms (SLO) for the primary chat endpoint.
- Average tokens per request (post-processing incl.): 480 tokens (we used a 512-rounding in the sheet).
- Baseline model: redwood-v2-7B-int4 (quantized) for steady state; fallback: redwood-v2-13B-fp16 when quality requires it.

Tokens -> throughput math (examples in spreadsheet):
- Customer commit: 45M tokens/month (~1.5M tokens/day).
- Expected average tokens/sec (steady regional distribution): ~17 tokens/sec sustained per qps spike window (this maps differently when you convert from requests/sec depending on tokens per request).
- For modeling: we used 512 tokens/request => ~2,930 requests/day => burst windows require ~35 concurrent decodes at 95th percentile.

GPU sizing (conservative, 25% headroom):
- redwood-v2-7B-int4: ~2200 tokens/sec per A100-80GB-equivalent slab when using 64-token micro-batches and warmed KV cache.
- To cover a 95th token demand of 70k tokens/sec (global burst), we recommend reserving 32 A100-simulated slots (8-node slab of 4 each) — this includes a 25% operational headroom and a small buffer for cold-starts.
- If we keep a portion on the 13B-fp16 (higher quality) for canary/fallback, add 6 x A100 slots to absorb degradation and fallbacks.

Optimizations that materially reduce GPU need (see tabs):
- Prefix KV caching for repeated context: 12–18% token reduction in hot paths.
- Dynamic batching: 20–30% better throughput in off-peak as long as latency windows accept a 5–8ms add.
- Quantized 7B model vs 13B: ~2.5x tokens/sec advantage on same hardware.

Attachments: sentinel_modeling_v2.xlsx (sheets: assumptions, burst-scenarios, fallback-costs), sla_scenarios.pdf (p95/p99 tables), runbook_draft.md (ops steps for canary + fallback).

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal alignment on final slab counts and canary schedule (Ben/Karthik to confirm).
2) Send this to your procurement team with the commit-to-slabs table (we can map to a monthly reserved SKU/price).
3) Agree a 30-day canary window with a fallback-to-hosted option for degraded quality.

Lina — can you confirm the daily token distribution (UTC primacy vs US peak) and whether you want the 13B fallback enabled by default for the first 14 days? That toggles ~18% additional GPU.

Thanks —
Kimberly

Kim — quick read through the workbook, looks good. A few notes from ops perspective: 

- The 2200 tokens/sec/A100 number for the 7B-int4 line assumes sustained micro-batching at 64; that breaks down if request variance pushes us to 8-token micro-batches during tail events. We should model a 10% degradation in worst-case tail batching.
- For the 32 A100-equivalents baseline you proposed: can we split across two regions (us-west/us-east) to reduce RPO and offer regional fallback? That reduces single-region headroom but increases cross-region cost.
- Suggest we offer a 2-tier reserved plan in the commercial: (A) committed slab with 15% discount + emergency burst (pay-as-you-go) and (B) committed+canary where we pre-provision fallback 13B capacity at a smaller discount but with guaranteed warm-up.

I've added a 'stress-matrix' tab to sentinel_modeling_v2.xlsx with an alternate demand curve where cold-starts and KV-warmup are 0–12 hours. Under that curve, recommended baseline increases to 38 A100-equivalents.

Ben

Ben / Kim — filling in some throughput/latency trade-offs from the infra bench: 

Quoted for context:
> Kim: "redwood-v2-7B-int4: ~2200 tokens/sec per A100-80GB-equivalent slab when using 64-token micro-batches and warmed KV cache."

My additions: 
- Measured delta for 7B-int4 between 64 -> 16 micro-batch: throughput drops ~28%, p95 increases by ~12–18ms. If we can't guarantee 64, budget ~1700 tokens/sec as a conservative operational number.
- KV cache hit rate assumptions matter: 40% hit reduces effective compute by ~20% in live traffic; we should model a low and high hit-rate scenario.
- Fallback policy: route quality-sensitive inference to 13B-fp16 only after we detect >3 consecutive quality misses in a user session (this keeps fallback activation low). That strategy uses under 8% extra tokens/sec on observed trial traffic.

My recommended final slab: 
- Conservative plan (safe ops): 38 x A100-equivalents for 7B-int4 with regional split (20 / 18) + 6 x reserved 13B slots for fallback canaries.
- Optimized plan (if Sentinel enables aggressive KV + warmup): 28 x A100-equivalents + 4 x 13B fallback.

I'll sync with Priyom to push the numbers into the SLA table and produce a short one-page ops-runbook for the canary (will attach runbook_draft.md).

Karthik

--

Thanks everyone — this is helpful and answers most of our follow-ups. A few clarifications from procurement/architect side: 

1) Regional split: we prefer a 60/40 US primacy (us-east primary) rather than even split — please re-run the cost delta for that.
2) Can you produce a 30-day canary runbook that includes: warm-up checklist, KV priming steps, roll-back triggers (p95 > 350ms for 15 minutes), and an emergency fallback to hosted API (DocuSign link for that addendum would be helpful).
3) Pricing ask: show committed slab pricing and payg burst SKU in a single table so procurement can compare.

We can confirm whether fallback 13B is enabled by default within 24 hours. If enabled by default, please show the incremental cost and how it maps to tokens/day.
